node.statement: Put epsilon=K*eta and let x,y be contractions in B. Use only validated nodes 1.1.2 and 1.1.3: Delta and Upsilon are completely contractive, while Phi is completely contractive with diagonal range. The root hypotheses give ||Delta Upsilon-Phi||_cb<=epsilon and ||Upsilon Delta-I_B||_cb<=epsilon. Therefore Phi Delta-Delta=(Phi-Delta Upsilon)Delta+Delta(Upsilon Delta-I_B), so submultiplicativity and ||Delta||_cb<=1 give ||Phi Delta-Delta||_cb<=epsilon+epsilon=2*epsilon. Set a=Delta x, b=Delta y, a0=Phi Delta x, b0=Phi Delta y. Complete contractivity makes a,b,a0,b0 contractions; a0 and b0 are diagonal and hence [a0,b0]=0; and the just-derived estimate gives ||a-a0||,||b-b0||<=2*epsilon. Thus [a,b]=[a-a0,b]+[a0,b-b0], and ||[u,v]||<=2||u||||v|| yields ||[Delta x,Delta y]||<=2(2*epsilon)*1+2*1*(2*epsilon)=8*epsilon. Finally the root multiplicativity hypothesis applied to (x,y) and (y,x), together with contractivity of Upsilon, gives ||[x,y]||<=||xy-Upsilon(Delta x Delta y)||+||Upsilon([Delta x,Delta y])||+||Upsilon(Delta y Delta x)-yx||<=epsilon+8*epsilon+epsilon=10*epsilon. This proves node 1.3.1 without using pending nodes 1.1 or 1.2.
